title: Let's Encrypt TLS Challenge failing when behind a Traefik TCP Router
body: I have one public IP forwarding ports 80 and 443 to Server 1. Server 1 uses SNI-based TCP routers with TLS passthrough to send traffic to Traefik instances on Server 2 and Server 3, where Let's Encrypt is configured with the TLS challenge. On Traefik 3.0.0, certificate requests on the downstream servers fail with HTTP 400; after initially thinking only the www name failed, I found that all certificate requests fail. ACME works on Server 1, which faces the internet directly. This behavior started with v3.0.0-rc4, and downgrading the TCP router to v3.0.0-rc3 makes it work again.

symptoms_visible: On Traefik 3.0.0, every certificate request made by Server 2 or Server 3 behind my SNI-based TLS-passthrough router fails with error 400.
Certificate requests work on the internet-facing Server 1, and the downstream requests work again when I downgrade the TCP router from v3.0.0-rc4 to v3.0.0-rc3.
N0.label: N0 downstream TLS challenges fail

symptoms_visible: The downstream TLS challenge still fails through the affected TCP router versions.
In another affected setup, using Traefik 2.11.0 for the TCP router restores certificate issuance, while 2.11.2 breaks it.
N1.label: N1 regression confirmed across release lines

symptoms_visible: TLS-ALPN certificate requests for downstream services still fail even though their matching TCP routers have TLS passthrough enabled.
I need the same gateway to obtain certificates for some of its own routes and to pass other TLS connections to services that manage their own certificates.
N2.label: N2 mixed gateway requirements established

symptoms_visible: After migrating my instances to DNS-01, my certificate requests succeed.
In the affected mixed setups, TLS-ALPN challenges still cannot pass through the gateway on the newer versions without changing the gateway behavior.
N3.label: N3 DNS-01 workaround applied

symptoms_visible: With the provided development branch, the downstream TLS challenge passes through the gateway and certificate issuance works.
N4.label: N4 candidate behavior verified

symptoms_visible: After enabling ACME bypass on the websecure entry point in a build containing the fix, downstream TLS-ALPN challenges follow the matching TCP passthrough router and certificates are issued successfully.
N_terminal.label: terminal TLS challenge passthrough restored

question_patterns: Does the same behavior occur on the Traefik 2.11 release line?
Which exact gateway versions work and fail in another affected setup?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I see the same issue with 2.11.2. Going back to 2.11.0 for the Traefik TCP router fixes it for me.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails on 2.11.0 and rc3 too, so I cannot identify any working Traefik version with this configuration.
The same boundary appears in my other setup: 2.11.2 fails and 2.11.0 works, but I did not test 2.11.1.

edges.comment: Comments c2-c3 came from a second affected user and are folded into the simulated user side. The answer reports only observed version behavior.

question_patterns: Is a TLS challenge resolver configured on the internet-facing gateway itself?
Does the gateway obtain certificates for any routes that it terminates locally?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. My external Traefik also has a TLS resolver enabled for some routes that it handles itself.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No. The gateway never obtains certificates or terminates TLS; it only forwards TCP connections.

question_patterns: What must happen for the routes sent to downstream Traefik instances or other TLS services?
Do the downstream services need to complete their own TLS-ALPN challenges?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Most traffic goes through TLS-passthrough to internal Traefik instances or appliances that manage their own TLS and need to complete their own challenges.

question_patterns: Would omitting the TLS resolver from the gateway configuration solve your use case?
Can the internet-facing Traefik run without its own TLS challenge resolver?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No, that would not fit my mixed setup because the external Traefik also resolves certificates for some local routes. I need it to keep doing that while passing other TLS challenges downstream.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes. This gateway is passthrough-only, so I can remove its TLS resolver without losing any local certificate handling.
I could separate the static configurations, but I still prefer one gateway that supports both local resolution and downstream passthrough.

edges.comment: The mixed-use answers combine the reporter's confirmation with affected users' detailed topology in c11-c22. All affected users are folded into one simulated user side. A static bypass option was volunteered as an acceptable compromise.

solution.intent: Avoid the blocked TLS-ALPN path by migrating certificate issuance to the DNS-01 challenge as a successful workaround.
solution.concrete_example: Configure the affected certificate resolvers to use DNS-01 instead of tlsChallenge so validation no longer has to traverse the gateway's TLS-ALPN routing path.

edges.comment: The reporter migrated to DNS-01 in c19 and stated that it solved the immediate certificate problem. This is a successful workaround, but it does not restore the TLS-passthrough behavior required by the other folded affected setups.

question_patterns: Could you test the provided development branch with the original downstream TLS challenge setup and report what happens?
Please try the candidate build against a passthrough route and tell me whether downstream certificate issuance works.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the development branch, and the passthrough is working like a charm. The downstream challenge completes successfully.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The development branch still intercepts the challenge, and downstream certificate issuance fails exactly as before.
The development branch works for my downstream Traefik route, although I tested only one hostname.

edges.comment: Comment c24 is a pre-landing test by another affected user, folded into the simulated user side. The user reports only the observed result; identifying the new entry-point behavior and its implementation remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Use the new entry-point ACME bypass switch so ACME TLS traffic can enter normal router matching and traverse TLS-passthrough routes, even when the gateway has its own certificate resolver.
solution.concrete_example:
On a Traefik build containing #10981, enable the option on the public TLS entry point:
entryPoints:
  websecure:
    address: ":443"
    allowACMEByPass: true

Keep `tls.passthrough: true` on the relevant TCP routers. Then retest certificate issuance through that entry point and confirm that the downstream resolver completes its TLS-ALPN challenge.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers mapped the version boundary to the behavior introduced by #10536: ACME TLS traffic was diverted to Traefik's internal ACME handler before ordinary TCP router matching, so `tls.passthrough` alone could not forward the challenge. #10981 added the `allowACMEByPass` entry-point option to permit that traffic to follow normal router selection. Those conclusions are engineer-side inference, not facts supplied by the reporter's version tests.

edges.comment: The implemented resolution was #10981. The option is per entry point, not per router. Post-fix verification should use a build containing the landed change without naming the implementation in the verification question.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: the ACME handling change introduced by #10536 preempted normal TCP router selection for TLS-ALPN challenges, so affected Traefik versions intercepted the challenge instead of honoring the matching TLS-passthrough route.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the observed version boundaries (3.0.0-rc3 versus rc4 and 2.11.0 versus 2.11.2), the mixed gateway topology, and the successful development-branch test.
The product fix must enable `allowACMEByPass: true` on the relevant entry point so ACME traffic can follow normal router matching and reach downstream services through TLS passthrough.
Must not claim that setting `tls.passthrough: true` alone fixes affected versions; it was already configured while all downstream TLS challenges failed.
Must not present removal of the gateway's TLS resolver as the full solution for this mixed setup, because the gateway also obtains certificates for routes it terminates locally.
DNS-01 may be offered as the reporter's successful workaround, but it must not be confused with restoration of downstream TLS-ALPN passthrough.
Must ask the user to verify certificate issuance on a build containing the fix before declaring the passthrough issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced self-hosting and network administrator who operates several Traefik instances, understands SNI routing, TLS passthrough, ACME challenge types, Docker configuration, and version rollback testing.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and configuration-focused; supplies concrete YAML and version boundaries, corrects the initial symptom report, and confirms practical workarounds concisely. Other affected operators are folded into the same user side for mixed-topology and test-build evidence.
